title: Plugins epic: gRPC plugin protocol + openclaw compat shim
description: Talon's drop-in goal requires supporting both (a) existing openclaw Node.js plugins from dist/extensions/ and (b) new native-language plugins (Go, Rust, Python, ...). Mechanism: subprocess plugins exposing a gRPC service. Each plugin runs as its own process; talon manages lifecycle (spawn, handshake, health, restart on crash) and dials the plugin's gRPC server. Hashicorp go-plugin is the canonical library for this pattern but we can roll a thin custom version if it's overkill. Existing openclaw extensions are reached via a special 'openclaw-plugin-host' subprocess (Node.js) that loads their JS via openclaw's loader and translates their hooks to our gRPC service — drops-in for the user's current channels (telegram), tools (brave), and providers (anthropic-via-claude-cli) without requiring rewrites.
close_reason: Closed

title: sessions.patch + sessions.list + sessions.subscribe; per-session model override in chat.send
description: The UI fails to change models with 'unknown method: sessions.patch'. Implement: (1) sessions.patch {key, model?, thinkingLevel?, verboseLevel?, fastMode?} stores a per-session prefs map; treats explicit null as 'clear'. (2) sessions.list returns the openclaw envelope {ts, path, count, defaults, sessions[]} including any sessions that have been patched OR have chat history. (3) sessions.subscribe is a no-op {ok:true} so the UI's subscribe call doesn't error; live presence events come later. (4) chat.send consults SessionPrefs.model BEFORE resolving the agent's PrimaryModel — UI override wins, provider derived from the override's ModelID. Other patch fields (thinkingLevel/verboseLevel/fastMode) are stored but not yet wired into chat.send.
close_reason: sessions.{patch,list,subscribe} land + per-session model override is honored by chat.send. SessionStore (sessionKey → SessionPref{Fields:map[string]json.RawMessage,UpdatedAt}) is mutex-guarded for concurrent reads from chat goroutines while the UI patches. Patch fields are stored as raw JSON so we can accept any patch shape openclaw's UI sends; explicit null clears a field. Helper SessionStore.Model(key) is called by ChatHandler.runStream BEFORE PrimaryModel resolution — UI override wins; provider derived from the override's ModelID.Provider() so model-switching across providers (openai → deepseek) Just Works. sessions.patch returns {ok,path,key,entry} mirroring openclaw's SessionsPatchResultBase. sessions.list returns {ts,path,count,defaults,sessions[]} (SessionsListResult shape) and includes both patched sessions and chat-only sessions (via ChatStore.Keys()). sessions.subscribe is a no-op {ok:true} — live presence events come later. Tests: store patch+null-clear, model helper, snapshot-is-a-copy, sessions.patch happy + missing-key, sessions.list combined source, subscribe ack, chat.send override wins, no-override uses default, compat for sessions.patch result shape.

title: agent.identity.get: accept sessionKey param (UI doesn't send agentId)
description: The openclaw web UI calls agent.identity.get with {sessionKey} (controllers/assistant-identity.ts: 'const params = sessionKey ? { sessionKey } : {}'). Our handler requires agentId and returns BAD_REQUEST. The UI's try/catch swallows the error silently, so the chat label sticks on the boot default 'Assistant' instead of resolving to 'Clawdia'. Fix: accept agentId OR sessionKey OR neither (default to 'main' — matching openclaw's resolveDefaultAgentId fallback). Derive agentId from sessionKey via the existing AgentIDFromSessionKey helper. Add a compat test that locks the request shape.
close_reason: agent.identity.get now resolves the agent in three tiers: explicit agentId → derived from sessionKey via AgentIDFromSessionKey → default 'main'. Mirrors openclaw's resolveDefaultAgentId fallback. Fixes the silent-failure bug where the UI's controllers/assistant-identity.ts call ('agent.identity.get', {sessionKey}) hit our agentId-required handler, got BAD_REQUEST, the catch swallowed it, and the chat label never updated from 'Assistant' to 'Clawdia'. Compat test added: TestCompat_AgentIdentityGetAcceptsSessionKeyParam locks the contract; sessionKey-only request must succeed and return the workspace IDENTITY.md name. Three additional unit tests cover no-params-defaults-to-main, all three sessionKey forms, and explicit agentId winning over sessionKey.

title: openai: empty content serialized as null breaks 400
description: OpenAI returned 'Invalid value for content: expected a string, got null' on a message[44] (tool result with empty output OR assistant turn with only tool_calls). buildRequestBody used omitempty on Content, dropping the field for empty strings; OpenAI maps missing content to null and rejects. Fix: drop omitempty on Content so it's always emitted as a string.
close_reason: Dropped omitempty on Content in oaiMessage so the field always serializes as a string (empty when no text). Tool result turns with no output and assistant-only-tool_calls turns now produce {role,content:'',tool_calls:[...]} or {role:'tool',tool_call_id,content:''} — both shapes OpenAI accepts. Regression test TestStream_EmptyContentIsExplicitStringNotNull asserts content:'' is present and content:null never appears.

title: gateway: port openclaw protocol v4 (chat delta shape + version bump)
description:
After merging upstream openclaw, MIN_CLIENT_PROTOCOL_VERSION=4 so the control UI sends {minProtocol:4,maxProtocol:4}. talon's gateway hardcodes ProtocolVersion=3 and rejects every connect with PROTOCOL_MISMATCH. Browser shows generic 'Could not connect'.

Port:
- internal/server/protocol.go: ProtocolVersion 3 -> 4
- internal/gateway/client.go: protocolVersion 3 -> 4
- internal/server/chat.go chatEventPayload: add DeltaText (required on delta state), Replace (optional, signals non-prefix replacement), StopReason (optional, on final/aborted). All omitempty so non-delta variants don't violate v4's additionalProperties:false.
- emitChat call sites: delta passes d.Text as deltaText (provider abstraction is append-only so replace is never set); final passes empty deltaText.

The message-action rename (inboundEventKind -> inboundTurnKind) is a no-op for talon: no current usage.

Source: openclaw commits 150bebcd0c, ad155fbbd7, 3f815fad12.

title: Plugins: replace bespoke host/spawn layer with hashicorp/go-plugin for first-party Go plugins
description: Talon's plugin layer (internal/plugin/* + internal/pluginrun/, ~3,300 LOC incl. tests) is a hand-rolled near-port of hashicorp/go-plugin: stdout handshake line, magic-cookie env var, subprocess+gRPC over loopback, host owns lifecycle. Swap it for the actual library for first-party Go plugins. Saves the bespoke-protocol maintenance, picks up AutoMTLS, plugin.Client lifecycle, hclog logging, GRPCBroker for bidi, ManagedClient reattach, and version negotiation for free. Node shim path (openclaw-bundled extensions) keeps the bespoke protocol for now under internal/plugin/legacy/ — see followup issues.
design:
Bifurcate internal/plugin. internal/plugin/pb stays untouched (Plugin + Host services keep their RPCs). internal/plugin/legacy/ is the current spawn/handshake/host/channels/provider/tools/image_provider code, package-renamed and used only by the Node shim path (openclaw-bundled extensions). internal/plugin/native/ is new go-plugin-based host+serve, used by first-party Go plugins. internal/pluginrun/ deletes; its only caller (cmd/talon/plugin_run.go) re-targets native.Serve.

Decisions: scope is first-party Go plugins only (deepseek, telegram, brave, whisper, bluebubbles, mac-notify); host callbacks via go-plugin GRPCBroker (one connection, no separate hostAddr listener); AutoMTLS on; apps/talon-*-plugin/ thin wrappers deleted (bin/talon covers them via talon plugin run <name>).

Components: native/grpcplugin.go implements plugin.GRPCPlugin — GRPCServer(broker, s) registers pb.RegisterPluginServer and stashes the broker; GRPCClient stashes broker on the host side. native/serve.go wraps plugin.Serve with talon HandshakeConfig (protocol version 1, magic cookie env var) so plugin authors don't see go-plugin types. native/host.go wraps plugin.NewClient with AutoMTLS + hclog->slog adapter + the resolvePluginCmd sibling/PATH fallback moved up from legacy into internal/plugin/pkgutil/. native/hostsvc.go implements pb.HostServer with identity bound from the broker connection (not a cookie) — broker.AcceptAndServe gets a per-plugin pb.HostServer instance so capability checks know which plugin is calling. cmd/talon/plugin_run.go and (briefly) apps/talon-*-plugin/main.go swap pluginrun.Serve -> native.Serve before apps/ deletes entirely.

Bidi flow: host.LoadPlugin -> plugin.NewClient(...).Start() forks+execs with auto-mTLS, broker comes up. Host calls broker.NextId() then broker.AcceptAndServe(N, register pb.HostServer scoped to this plugin). conn := client.Client() returns the gRPC conn to the plugin's server; host sends Initialize with HostBrokerId=N. Plugin's Initialize handler runs broker.Dial(req.HostBrokerId) to get a ClientConn it wraps with pb.NewHostClient for callbacks, then returns its manifest. auth_cookie and host_address fields in InitializeRequest become deprecated, kept on the wire for one release for shim back-compat.

gateway_chat.go:collectPluginSpecs gets a Kind field per spec: BuiltinPluginCmd -> native, bundled (shim) -> legacy, explicit cmd -> legacy (preserves third-party back-compat). plugin_deps.go's BuiltinPluginCmd unchanged.

Error handling: plugin.Client.Exited() drives host.Unregister via a watcher goroutine (1:1 with current behavior). mTLS handshake failures surface from plugin.NewClient.Start() as typed errors. Capability denials still enforced inside hostsvc methods. Plugin stderr routes through the hclog->slog adapter at the level go-plugin emits.

Testing: internal/plugin/native/host_test.go drives a fresh native/testplugin/ binary through Initialize -> RunTool -> host callback -> Shutdown. Existing internal/plugin/*_test.go move into legacy/ with package rename, otherwise unchanged. internal/plugins/*/plugin_test.go should be transport-agnostic and need zero changes (verify). cmd/talon/gateway_plugins_test.go asserts Kind=native for first-party entries.

Migration steps: (1) add hashicorp/go-plugin to go.mod, vet; (2) move internal/plugin/{spawn,handshake,host,channels,provider,tools,image_provider}.go + tests into internal/plugin/legacy/, rename package, fix every importer; (3) hoist resolvePluginCmd into internal/plugin/pkgutil/resolve.go; (4) scaffold internal/plugin/native/ to compile; (5) wire native.Serve into cmd/talon/plugin_run.go; (6) implement native.Host.LoadPlugin with GRPCBroker; (7) implement native/hostsvc.go porting capability-gated handlers from legacy; (8) update collectPluginSpecs Kind dispatch in gateway_chat.go; (9) delete apps/talon-*-plugin/ and corresponding Makefile/CI bits; (10) integration-test one plugin end-to-end, then all six; (11) delete internal/pluginrun/; (12) update CLAUDE.md if it references the deleted paths.

Out of scope (each its own follow-up): Node shim port (openclaw-plugin-host implements go-plugin HandshakeConfig in Go, then legacy/ deletes); auto-mTLS cert pinning / protocol version negotiation policy; third-party plugin docs.
acceptance_criteria: github.com/hashicorp/go-plugin is in go.mod; internal/plugin/native/ replaces internal/pluginrun/ for the talon plugin run dispatcher; all six first-party plugins (deepseek/telegram/brave/whisper/bluebubbles/mac-notify) spawn through go-plugin with AutoMTLS; host->plugin (RunTool/StreamCompletion/etc.) and plugin->host (GetConfig/RunSubagent/etc.) RPCs both work end-to-end via GRPCBroker; apps/talon-*-plugin/ and internal/pluginrun/ deleted; bespoke spawn/handshake/host code moved to internal/plugin/legacy/ and exercised only by the Node shim; existing internal/plugins/*/plugin_test.go pass without modification; go test ./... is green; CLAUDE.md updated for any moved/deleted paths.

title: Plugins: native Go bluebubbles channel plugin (iMessage via BlueBubbles)
description:
Native Go counterpart to the openclaw extensions/bluebubbles JS extension. Mirrors apps/talon-telegram-plugin shape: subprocess gRPC plugin offering channel='bluebubbles'. iMessage via the user's BlueBubbles Server Helper (Mac app + REST + webhooks).

V1 scope (this issue):
- Inbound: HTTP webhook listener on a configurable local port. User points BlueBubbles webhook at http://<host>:<port>/webhook. Parses 'new-message' events and emits pb.IncomingChannelMessage on the StartChannel stream.
- Outbound: SendChannelMessage POSTs to <serverUrl>/api/v1/message/text?password=<password> with {chatGuid, message, tempGuid, method:'private-api'}. RoomID round-trips as chatGuid.
- Tool: bluebubbles_send so the agent can proactively message a known chat.
- Config (channels.bluebubbles.* sub-tree, passed via StartChannelRequest.channel_config):
  serverUrl (string), password (string — secret resolution by host), webhookPort (int), dmPolicy ('pairing'|'allowlist'|'open'|'disabled'), allowFrom ([]string of handle addresses), groupPolicy, groupAllowFrom.
- BuiltinPluginCmd registration (internal/server/plugin_deps.go) so the entry can be enabled with bare {enabled: true}.
- Makefile PLUGINS list entry.
- Dockerfile build/copy steps.

V2/deferred:
- Reactions, edits, unsend, replies (channels.bluebubbles.actions.*).
- Attachments (mediaMaxMb, mediaLocalRoots).
- catchup (poll history on startup).
- Group enrichment from contacts.
- Setup wizard parity (channels.bluebubbles.verify/captureSender/persist RPCs).
- Schema parity with extensions/bluebubbles/openclaw.plugin.json (the JS plugin has ~50 config keys; we ship the load-bearing ~10 for v1).

Reference: extensions/bluebubbles/ has the JS plugin's bundled output; extensions/bluebubbles/openclaw.plugin.json has the full config schema.

title: Plugins: self-dispatching binary so first-party plugins ship as 'talon plugin run <name>'
description: Today first-party plugins are separate binaries (apps/talon-deepseek-plugin, etc.) that only get installed inside the Docker image at /usr/local/bin/talon-*-plugin. Non-Docker users (Homebrew, go install, raw checkouts) have no story to install them. The remaining proper fix: refactor each apps/talon-*-plugin/main.go to expose its serving logic as a reusable function, then add a 'talon plugin run <name>' subcommand that dispatches to it. The four hardcoded /usr/local/bin/talon-*-plugin defaults (internal/server/plugin_deps.go builtinPlugins, cmd/talon/configure.go:158, internal/server/channels_setup.go:50) flip to self-referential cmds: [<talon-binary>, plugin, run, <name>]. Net result: one binary covers gateway plus all first-party plugins; Homebrew/go install/Docker all work without a per-plugin install dance. Third-party plugins keep using the existing subprocess-with-cmd protocol — this only changes how the bundled ones ship.

title: Host service implementation: capability-gated plugin → host RPCs
description: Implement pb.HostServer methods (GetConfig, ListAgents, GetAgentIdentity, ListModels, ListSessions, GetChatHistory, AppendMemory, RunSubagent) by adapting talon's existing handlers (ReadHandler, ChatHandler, SessionsHandler, memory.Append). Spin up a separate gRPC listener at gateway startup, register HostService with the Host's UnaryInterceptor + StreamInterceptor for capability gating, advertise the listen address to plugins via plugin.NewHost(addr) so loaded plugins can dial back. server.Server gains ChatHandler/ChatStore/SessionStore accessors so cmd/talon can wire HostService against the same shared state the WS surface uses. Out of scope: streaming-completion forwarding (StreamCompletion is on Plugin service, host calls plugin not vice versa); channel send (still in talon-13z).

Each method delegates to the existing in-process handler logic (ReadHandler.handleConfigGet, handleAgentsList, handleAgentIdentityGet, handleModelsList; SessionsHandler.handleList; ChatHandler.handleHistory + RunInline; memory.Append) so plugins see the same shape and same data the WS surface does — no drift between UI and plugin views. AppendMemory resolves agentId → workspace via the same three-tier precedence as the WS memory.append. server.Server gained ChatHandler/ChatStore/SessionStore/ReadHandler accessors (chat may be nil; reads always non-nil with paths fallback). cmd/talon/gateway.go: net.Listen ephemeral 127.0.0.1:0 → plugin.NewHost(addr) → server.New (so handlers exist) → NewHostService wiring → grpc.NewServer with Host UnaryInterceptor + StreamInterceptor → goroutine Serve → loadConfiguredPlugins (so plugins dial back into a live host service) → defer pluginHost.Shutdown + grpcSrv.GracefulStop. title: Plugins: subprocess host runtime in talon
description: Lifecycle manager for plugin subprocesses. description: The openclaw web UI's config screens call config.get to populate forms (auth, channels, models, plugins, etc.). Without it, those views error out. title: Subagents: parallel agent invocation primitive
description: Allow the active agent to delegate work to a subagent in parallel. openclaw's setup has multiple configured agents (main, coding, research, deepwork) — each with its own model/workspace. We need: (1) 'subagent' tool that takes {agentId, prompt} and runs that agent's chat.send loop, returns the final text. (2) Parallel scheduling: when the model calls subagent multiple times in one turn, run them concurrently with bounded parallelism. (3) Result aggregation as tool results so the parent's multi-turn loop continues. ADK is a candidate runtime — its multi-agent orchestration covers (1)+(2) out of the box but adds a heavy abstraction layer. Native implementation reuses our existing chat.send + ChatStore + tool registry. Decision: native first to preserve speed; ADK reconsidered if we hit a missing primitive (planner, hierarchical agents, etc).
close_reason: Subagent tool + parallel multi-tool execution. Refactored chat.runStream into a thin goroutine wrapper around runChatLoop(ctx, sess, ...) which now returns (finalText, error). Adds ChatHandler.RunInline(ctx, agentID, message) that runs the full multi-turn loop with sess=nil under a fresh sessionKey 'subagent:<agentID>:<runId>'; events fire to no-one and the accumulated text is returned to the caller. Subagent tool in internal/tools delegates to a SubagentRunner interface (ChatHandler satisfies it). tools.NewWithSubagent(workspace, runner) registers the subagent tool alongside the builtins. Recursion is bounded by maxSubagentDepth=3 via a context-value depth counter; subagent tool refuses to fire when the limit is hit. server.Config.ToolRunnerFor signature gained a SubagentRunner argument; cmd/talon's makeToolRunner passes it through to tools.NewWithSubagent. Parallel tool execution: when the model emits multiple tool calls in one turn, runToolsParallel dispatches them concurrently with maxToolConcurrency=4; results are appended to ChatStore in original call order so the next turn's history is deterministic. Single-call path stays sequential to avoid goroutine overhead. Tests: tools subagent (delegate, missing args, depth limit, nil-runner skips, registered alongside builtins); RunInline (happy path with subagent session in store, empty-args rejection, provider error propagation); 3-tool parallel run completes in ~50ms not 150ms with maxActive≥2.

title: Memory: 'remember' tool + memory.append RPC

Appends to <workspace>/memory/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md (creates with H1 header on first write of the day). (2) memory.append RPC {agentId|sessionKey, text} for non-chat clients. Both share the same writer. Emits an agent.tool stream event (phase=start with text, phase=result acknowledging the write) so the UI shows the write in the tool stream. No structured store, no recall — those land later. Depends on the workspace/memory loader (talon-?) so writes are immediately visible on the next chat.send.

Extend it to also walk <workspace>/memory/, sort filenames descending (newest first), and inject the most recent N entries below the canonical context files. Skips non-markdown files, blank-only entries, and missing memory/ dirs gracefully. title: Openclaw compat regression test suite

title: Gateway dedups sessions by clientId+instanceId on connect
description: A single UI page-load opens two simultaneous WS connections to talon-gateway (visible as two adjacent 'ws connected conn=...' log lines on the same remote IP, different ports). Likely UI-side: Lit connectedCallback firing twice on HMR or connectGateway racing with the deferred bootstrap finally. The gateway should defend against this regardless: when a new connect handshake completes with the same client.id + client.instanceId as an active session, close the older session with a structured reason (e.g. 'replaced-by-newer-instance'). Implementation: server tracks active sessions in a sync.Map keyed by 'clientId|instanceId'. After hello-ok, register; on session exit, deregister; if a key already exists, signal the old session to shut down via a context-cancel channel.
close_reason: Gateway dedups WS sessions by clientId+instanceId at end of handshake. Server tracks active sessions in a sync.Mutex-guarded map keyed by '<clientId>|<instanceId>'. Session.register inserts after hello-ok; if the key was occupied the old session.shutdown is called (StatusNormalClosure with reason 'replaced-by-newer-instance') so the displaced WS gets a clean close-frame the UI can interpret. Session.deregister uses compare-and-delete so the displaced session's defer doesn't accidentally remove its successor on the way out. Empty clientId or instanceId skips registration (CLI/no-instance clients still work, just without dedup). Tests cover: same-key replacement evicts old, different-instanceIds coexist (multi-tab), CAS prevents stale deregister, empty key is a no-op, 100-goroutine concurrent register/unregister doesn't deadlock.

title: Tools: chat event payload supports tool_use + tool_result content blocks
description: The openclaw web UI's app-tool-stream renders tool calls and results from chat event content blocks: {type:'tool_use', id, name, input} and {type:'tool_result', tool_use_id, content:[{type:'text',text:...}]}. chat events emitted by talon-gateway need to include those blocks so the UI tool stream shows live progress. Per tool call: emit a chat event with state=delta and a content block with type=tool_use as soon as we begin executing; emit a follow-up with type=tool_result once the tool returns. Final assistant message in chat.history should also carry the assembled blocks so refreshes restore the visual.
close_reason: Tool execution emits openclaw 'agent' events with stream='tool' so the UI's app-tool-stream renders the in-flight tool card and result. Per tool call: emitAgentToolStart fires {data:{toolCallId,name,phase:'start',args:<parsed JSON or raw>}} before runner.Run, emitAgentToolResult fires {data:{toolCallId,name,phase:'result',result:<output>}} after. RunID matches the chat runId (since talon uses the client's idempotencyKey as the runId, the UI can correlate tool events back to the active chat run unlike openclaw's runtime which uses a different engine-side runId). Build helpers are pure functions tested independently: parsed-JSON args, fallback-to-raw-string on malformed JSON, result passthrough. Out of scope (talon-iod): approval prompts and exec policy.

title: Tools: multi-turn loop in chat.send
description: chat.send currently does a single provider stream then emits state=final. With tools enabled, the loop becomes: stream → on each DeltaToolCall, run the tool via the registry → append tool_result message → re-call provider with the updated history → repeat until the stream terminates with no tool_calls. Cap at MaxToolIterations (default 16) to avoid runaway loops; if the cap is hit emit state=error with errorKind='tool-loop-limit'. ChatStore message shape grows to support tool_use and tool_result content blocks (still text for plain user/assistant turns). Tests with stub provider that emits a tool_call on first stream and text on second confirm the multi-turn cycle, the iteration cap, and the proper history shape feeding back into the second call.
close_reason: Multi-turn loop landed in chat.send. Per chat.send: build tool runner once (workspace via WorkspaceResolver, registry via ToolRunnerFor factory) → iterate up to MaxToolIterations (default 16): build messages from store, attach Registry.Specs() as Request.Tools, stream → on DeltaText accumulate + emit cumulative state=delta, on DeltaToolCall buffer; when stream ends with toolCalls → AppendAssistantWithCalls + run each tool sequentially (errors captured into result string) + AppendToolResult, loop back; with no toolCalls → Append assistant text + emit state=final and return. Cap exhaustion emits state=error with errorKind='tool-loop-limit'. Model invoking tools without a configured runner emits state=error with errorKind='tool-runner-unavailable' (rather than ignoring the call and looping forever). Text-only chat without WithTools regresses to the previous single-turn behavior. ChatStore extended: AppendAssistantWithCalls (assistant turn with tool_calls), AppendToolResult (role=tool with ToolCallID). messagesFromHistory translates store rows to provider.Messages preserving tool_calls and ToolCallID. Server config grew WorkspaceResolver + ToolRunnerFor; cmd/talon wires both via configAgentResolver (also implements WorkspaceResolver now) and tools.New(workspace). Tests with scriptedProvider + stubToolRunner cover: full call → execute → re-stream cycle with correct history shape, iteration cap stops at MaxToolIterations, tool-runner-unavailable errors out cleanly, text-only mode regression.

title: Tools: builtin tool registry + read/write/bash/grep/glob impls
description: internal/tools package: Tool interface (Name, Description, ParametersSchema, Run(ctx, input json.RawMessage) (output, error)). Builtins, all workspace-scoped (paths resolved relative to a Workspace string passed at registry construction; absolute paths are rejected unless they resolve under workspace): read (file contents, line range), write (create/overwrite), edit (find/replace by string match), bash (exec a command via /bin/sh -c with timeout, capture stdout+stderr), glob (workspace-relative pattern), grep (regex over files). Each tool has a JSON schema for parameters. Registry exposes ListSpecs() []provider.ToolSpec and Run(ctx, name, input) (output, error). Tests against a temp workspace cover the workspace-confinement guard.
close_reason: internal/tools package landed. Tool interface (Name/Description/ParametersSchema/Run), Registry rooted at a workspace, Specs() returns []provider.ToolSpec ready to attach to a Request. Six builtin tools, all workspace-confined: read (with optional line range), write (creates parent dirs), edit (errors on ambiguous or missing match — echoes Claude Code's edit semantics), bash (CombinedOutput, default 30s/max 5min timeout, exit code in trailer, cwd=workspace), glob (filepath.Glob, workspace-relative results), grep (regex via WalkDir, max 200 matches, skips .git/node_modules/.talon, supports include glob filter). resolveInWorkspace uses filepath.Rel to reject path traversal and lookalike-prefix attacks (workspace=/foo, target=/foobar/x is rejected). 23 tests cover the registry surface, every tool's happy path, traversal rejection, ambiguous-match error, exit code formatting, and context cancellation tolerance.

title: Tools: provider interface tool support + OpenAI tool-call streaming
description: Add tool support to provider.Provider: (1) Request.Tools []ToolSpec advertising available tools to the model, (2) new Delta variant DeltaToolCall carrying {id, name, argsJSON} once a call's args have fully arrived. OpenAI impl: serialize tools into the request body shape (tools:[{type:'function',function:{name,description,parameters}}]), parse the streamed delta.tool_calls[].function.{name,arguments} fragments by index, accumulate args as JSON-stringified fragments per index, and emit one DeltaToolCall per completed call when finish_reason becomes 'tool_calls' or the stream ends. ToolSpec is a small struct {Name, Description, ParametersSchema json.RawMessage} so callers can pass any JSON-schema. Tests with httptest server using a recorded SSE transcript for tool-calls. Out of scope: actual tool execution; multi-turn loop.
close_reason: Provider interface gained tool support: Request.Tools []ToolSpec ({Name, Description, ParametersSchema}), DeltaToolCall variant carrying *ToolCall ({ID, Name, ArgumentsJSON}), Message extended with ToolCalls []ToolCall (assistant turn invoking tools) and ToolCallID string (role=tool result turns). RoleTool added. OpenAI provider serializes tools as tools:[{type:'function',function:{name,description,parameters}}], assistant tool_calls as tool_calls:[{id,type:function,function:{name,arguments}}], tool results as {role:tool,tool_call_id,content}. SSE pump accumulates per-index tool_call fragments (id+name on first chunk, args fragments thereafter) and flushes one DeltaToolCall per index when finish_reason='tool_calls' or stream ends. Tests: tool-call accumulation across 3 args fragments → single assembled call, request body includes tools field when set, tools omitted when absent, assistant tool_calls + tool result messages serialize correctly.

title: Native agent.identity.get on talon-gateway
description: The web UI calls agent.identity.get {agentId} to render the assistant's name + avatar in the chat header. Without it, every assistant message says 'Assistant' instead of the IDENTITY.md-derived name (e.g. 'Clawdia 🦞'). Implementation: resolve the agent's workspace from merged config (per-agent workspace field, fallback to agents.defaults.workspace), read <workspace>/IDENTITY.md, parse the markdown bullet list ('- **Name:** X', '- **Emoji:** Y', '- **Avatar:** Z'), return {agentId, name, emoji, avatar}. avatar may be a workspace-relative path, http(s) URL, or data URI. Missing IDENTITY.md returns null (UI tolerates null) so the chat header falls back to agent id.
close_reason: Native agent.identity.get on talon-gateway. Resolves agent's workspace from per-agent .workspace field with fallback to agents.defaults.workspace, then reads <workspace>/IDENTITY.md and parses the markdown bullet list ('- **Name:** X', '- **Emoji:** Y', '- **Avatar:** Z'). Returns {agentId, name, emoji, avatar} where avatar falls back to emoji when the field is empty (matches openclaw behavior). Unknown agents and missing IDENTITY.md return nil so the UI's null-tolerant path falls back to the agent id. Parser is tolerant of whitespace + key case, ignores italics-wrapped continuation hints like '_(workspace-relative path...)_'. Tests cover the real openclaw template format, filled-avatar shorthand, empty document, case/whitespace tolerance, defaults workspace fallback, unknown agent, missing IDENTITY.md, and missing agentId param.

title: talon-gateway: print UI deep-link on startup, add talon ui open
description: The gateway URL (ws://localhost:18790) is the single most-typed string in dev — and forgettable after a browser cache clear. title: Native chat.send + chat event stream (uses provider interface)
description: Implement chat.send and the chat event stream on talon-gateway. chat.send accepts {sessionKey, message, idempotencyKey} (matching openclaw shape) and: (1) resolves sessionKey to an agentId (default sessionKey form is agent:<agentId>:<agentId>), (2) loads that agent's primary model from merged config, (3) creates a Provider for the model's provider name (factory lookup), (4) launches a streaming completion in a goroutine, (5) fans Provider Deltas out to the originating session as 'chat' events with the openclaw event shape: {runId, sessionKey, seq, state:'streaming'|'final'|'aborted'|'error', message:{phase:'assistant',role:'assistant',content:[{type:'text',text:...}]}, errorKind?, errorMessage?}. Idempotency: if a runId is already active for {sessionKey, idempotencyKey} return the existing runId and replay events from a per-session ring buffer (cap 100 events) for late subscribers. Acceptance: openclaw web UI at http://localhost:5173/chat?session=main can send a message and watch tokens stream in when pointed at talon-gateway with the OpenAI provider configured. Depends on talon-ax2 (interface), talon-e21 (OpenAI impl).
close_reason: chat.send + chat event stream landed on talon-gateway. ChatHandler in internal/server/chat.go: parses sessionKey via AgentIDFromSessionKey('agent:<id>:<convo>' → '<id>'), resolves agent's primary model via AgentResolver, materializes provider via ProviderFactory, appends user msg to ChatStore (in-memory), then spawns a streaming goroutine that fans provider.Delta events out as openclaw-shaped 'chat' events (state: streaming|final|error; payload includes runId, sessionKey, seq, message.content[0].text). Idempotency: same {sessionKey, idempotencyKey} returns the existing runId. Session.PushEvent is now write-mutex serialized. cmd/talon/gateway_chat.go provides the concrete configAgentResolver (reads agents.list[].model.primary from merged config) and agentProviderFactory (loads openai:default api_key from <openclaw>/agents/<agentId>/agent/auth-profiles.json; only 'openai' is implemented). gateway run wires both into server.Config and logs 'chat=enabled, providers=openai'. Tests cover param validation, agent-not-found, provider-unavailable, missing provider segment, idempotency same-runId, distinct runIds without idempotency key, sessionKey parsing edge cases, ChatStore append+snapshot+isolation. Out of scope: ring-buffer replay for late subscribers, multi-provider, fallbacks, system prompts, tool use.

title: Native models.list RPC handler on talon-gateway
description: Wire the models.list registry handler in internal/server. Reads model definitions from talon's merged config (models.providers.<provider>.models[]) and returns the same envelope shape the openclaw gateway emits today: {models:[{id,name,provider,contextWindow,input:[modalities],reasoning,alias?},...]}. Independent of provider work — just a config read.
close_reason: Native agents.list, models.list, and config.schema landed on talon-gateway via internal/server/reads.go (ReadHandler). agents.list synthesizes the openclaw envelope shape (agents:[{id, model:{primary,fallbacks}, workspace?, name?}], defaultId, mainKey, scope) — primary resolves with the same three-tier precedence as configAgentResolver (per-agent .model.primary → per-agent .model string → agents.defaults.model.primary), and fallbacks come from defaults.model.fallbacks. defaultId prefers 'main' or falls back to the first agent. models.list flattens models.providers.<name>.models[] and decorates each row with the alias from agents.defaults.models[<key>].alias when present; sorted by id for stable output. config.schema returns the cached envelope at ~/.talon/cache/config-schema.json verbatim, with a helpful error message pointing at 'talon config schema --refresh' when the cache is missing or invalid. Tests cover model precedence, defaultId fallback, alias decoration, sort order, missing/invalid schema cache, and registry registration.

title: OpenAI provider implementation (streaming chat completions)
description: Concrete Provider implementation for OpenAI in internal/provider/openai. Reads the api_key from <openclaw>/agents/<agentId>/agent/auth-profiles.json under 'openai:default'. Calls https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions with stream=true; parses SSE; emits TextDelta per token chunk and FinalUsage on the [DONE] terminator. No tool-use, no function-calling, no JSON mode. Acceptance: integration test with a stub HTTP server that emits a recorded SSE transcript; provider produces the expected Delta sequence. Out of scope: rate-limit handling beyond surfacing errors. Depends on talon-ax2 (provider interface).
notes: The Anthropic OAuth profile in this project flows through Claude Code; that is intentionally NOT implemented in this issue — it is materially harder and tracked separately.
close_reason: OpenAI provider implementation in internal/provider/openai. Provider.Stream POSTs to /chat/completions with stream=true and stream_options.include_usage=true; SSE pump translates each data: chunk into a TextDelta and emits a final UsageDelta when the API reports it. Auth is plumbed via LoadAPIKey(authProfilesPath, profileID) which reads openclaw's auth-profiles.json and returns the openai:default api_key. Setup errors (missing key, non-openai provider segment, HTTP non-200) come back via the error return; mid-stream parse errors arrive as DeltaError followed by channel close. Tests with httptest server cover happy path (recorded SSE transcript: 'Hello, world' + 12/3 token usage), HTTP 401 surfacing, missing-key rejection, wrong-provider rejection, malformed-chunk → error delta. LoadAPIKey tests cover happy path, wrong-provider mismatch, oauth-type rejection, missing-profile error.

title: Provider interface (internal/provider package)
description: Design and ship the streaming-completion provider interface that talon-gateway's chat.send will use. Types only in this issue — no concrete provider impl. Goals: (1) define internal/provider/provider.go with a Provider interface that takes a streaming Request and returns a stream of Delta events; (2) Request shape: ModelID (the openclaw 'provider/model' form, e.g. openai/gpt-5.4-mini), Messages ([]Message with Role+Content), System string, Temperature/MaxTokens/etc as a generic Options; (3) Delta shape covers TextDelta, ReasoningDelta, FinalUsage (input/output tokens), and ErrorDelta; (4) Provider.Stream(ctx, req) returns (<-chan Delta, error). The provider implementation receives auth credentials separately (probably via a Credentials interface or a field on the provider struct returned by a Factory). Out of scope: actual HTTP/SDK calls, model catalogs, tool-use, multi-modal. Acceptance: types compile, interface is documented, a unit test exercises a stub provider that emits a fixed delta sequence to confirm channel semantics. Blocks talon-aws sub-work for chat.send (talon-aws-5) and OpenAI impl (talon-aws-2).
notes: User direction (2026-04-27): build the provider interface up-front, not bolted on after a hardcoded first-cut. Anthropic goes through Claude Code OAuth (claude-cli) so it is the *harder* provider; OpenAI is the simpler first concrete impl since it has a normal API key in auth-profiles.json.
close_reason: internal/provider package landed: Provider interface (Name() + Stream(ctx, Request) (<-chan Delta, error)), Request/Message/Options/ModelID types with Provider()/Model() helpers, Delta with DeltaKind discriminant (Text/Reasoning/Usage/Error) plus Usage. Stub provider for tests replays a recorded script, records calls, honors ctx cancel, terminates on DeltaError. Tests: ModelID split, in-order replay, channel close after error delta, prompt close on ctx cancel. Compile-time assertion that Stub satisfies Provider. Credentials are NOT in the interface — concrete providers handle their own auth (per design).

title: Gateway WS connect handshake (login)
description: Implement the openclaw-compatible WS connect handshake on claw-gateway so the control UI can log in. Spec (from openclaw client-kQ1-TM3I.js): server emits connect.challenge event with {nonce, ts} on connect. Client sends req method=connect with ConnectParamsSchema (minProtocol, maxProtocol, client.{id,version,platform,mode}, optional auth.{token,password,deviceToken,bootstrapToken}, role, scopes). Server replies with res payload shaped as hello-ok: {protocol, server.{version,connId}, features.{methods[], events[]}, snapshot.{presence[], health, stateVersion, uptimeMs, authMode?}, policy.{maxPayload, maxBufferedBytes, tickIntervalMs}, optional auth.{role, scopes[], issuedAtMs}}. Auth modes: none/token (skip password/trusted-proxy for now). Reject pre-connect frames except 'connect'. After connect, dispatch req frames to a registry; unknown methods return ErrorCodes shape.
acceptance_criteria: control UI can complete login against claw gateway; existing claw client connects without changes; unknown RPC methods return a structured error.
close_reason: Closed

title: Reuse single WS connection for sequential RPCs

title: First-run BOOTSTRAP onboarding flow (interactive identity setup)
description: Port openclaw's BOOTSTRAP.md onboarding pattern to talon. Static persona scaffolding now lands defaults on first run (internal/agentcontext/EnsureDefaults, wired in cmd/talon/gateway.go), but there is no interactive identity bootstrap.
design:
openclaw shipped a BOOTSTRAP.md sentinel: on the first conversation the agent read it, interviewed the user to fill IDENTITY.md/SOUL.md/USER.md, then deleted BOOTSTRAP.md. Its absence marked the workspace as initialized. talon references BOOTSTRAP.md only in comments; no code consumes or writes it (state machine never ported, removed with openclaw compat in commit b8a1943).

Scope for this issue:
1. Seed a BOOTSTRAP.md template alongside the existing defaults (write-if-missing) OR generate it as part of EnsureDefaults.
2. On chat startup, when BOOTSTRAP.md is present, fold its instructions into the system prompt so the agent runs the interview on the first turn.
3. Provide a tool/flow for the agent to write IDENTITY/SOUL/USER and then delete BOOTSTRAP.md (the 'initialized' signal).
4. Decide the trigger surface: only the main agent, only when files are still the untouched defaults, etc.

Likely needs an ADR (stateful onboarding flow touching chat path + workspace lifecycle). Builds on agentcontext.EnsureDefaults.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh install runs a one-time identity interview that populates IDENTITY/SOUL/USER and removes the BOOTSTRAP sentinel; second run does not re-trigger; existing customized workspaces are never re-onboarded.
close_reason: Implemented in commit d9c75d9 (ADR 0007). Fresh-install onboarding: gateway arms a BOOTSTRAP sentinel on a fresh main workspace; leading system-prompt directive drives an interactive interview; dedicated finish_onboarding tool writes IDENTITY.md/USER.md and clears the sentinel. Lifecycle layered in internal/agentcontext + wrapped as a tool in internal/agentcore_chat. Unit-tested (agentcontext + tool) and verified e2e: arms once, no re-arm on restart, stays cleared after completion. Remaining manual check (needs a live model+key): confirm the LLM actually conducts the interview and calls the tool on a real first chat — can't unit-test model adherence.

title: Port default mismatch: CLI defaults to 18789, gateway server defaults to 18790
description:
Pre-existing default mismatch between the talon CLI client and the embedded gateway server.

internal/config/config.go:159 — CLI client defaults to gateway.port = 18789 when not in config.
cmd/talon/gateway.go:297 — gateway run --port flag defaults to 18790.

Symptom: user runs 'talon gateway run' (no --port), CLI then runs any command, gets 'disconnected (1006): no reason' because the CLI dials 18789 and the gateway is on 18790. Diagnostic looks like a WebSocket bug; root cause is just the two numbers don't match.

Fix: pick one canonical default and use it both places. 18789 has more history (matches openclaw upstream and the existing CLI default config); 18790 was likely chosen for the gateway flag to avoid colliding with a running upstream openclaw on dev machines, but the comment doesn't say so. Recommend aligning on 18789 to match the CLI and openclaw, then if collision avoidance was the original intent, document it explicitly somewhere visible (CLAUDE.md or a constant comment).

Touch points if changing the default:
- cmd/talon/gateway.go:297 (gateway run --port flag default)
- cmd/talon/gateway.go:287 (host listener port for plugin gRPC, also defaults around here)
- Any tests that hardcode 18790 (grep across e2e + server tests)
notes: Resolved: aligned all defaults to 18789 (the UI default per openclaw/ui storage.ts:98). Changed: cmd/talon/gateway.go:297 (gateway run --port default 18790→18789), cmd/talon/dashboard.go:47 (port fallback 18790→18789), cmd/talon/ui.go:91 (--gateway-port flag default 18790→18789). Plus user overlay gateway.port set to 18789. The defaults-everywhere-must-match invariant now holds: CLI dialer 18789, gateway server 18789, dashboard URL 18789, UI default 18789. No more 'non-default gateway' warning when opening the dashboard. The 'gateway.url no-op' subfinding stays open (filed inline above) — config field is silently ignored; either implement it or reject unknown keys.

title: Logging: migrate from stdlib log to log/slog (structured, no external deps)
description:
Today: stdlib 'log' across 6 files, 21 call sites (cmd/talon/gateway.go, cmd/talon/gateway_chat.go, internal/plugin/spawn.go, internal/plugin/channels.go, internal/server/server.go, internal/server/chat.go). All log.Printf/Println/Fatalf, format-string-only, no fields.

Goal: migrate to log/slog (stdlib, no external dep). Default text handler for human reading; JSON handler optional for production. Surface is small enough to do in one pass.

Conversion pattern:
  log.Printf("plugin %s: load failed: %v", name, err)
  → slog.Error("plugin load failed", "plugin", name, "err", err)

  log.Printf("plugin %s: loaded — tools=%d providers=%d channels=%d", spec.name, t, p, c)
  → slog.Info("plugin loaded", "plugin", spec.name, "tools", t, "providers", p, "channels", c)

Considerations:
- internal/plugin/spawn.go forwardStdout currently does log.Printf("[plugin/%s] %s", name, line) for plugin subprocess stdout — want this to stay one-line-per-event but with the plugin name as a structured field, not embedded in the message.
- Plugin subprocesses (apps/talon-*-plugin/main.go) write to their own stderr today via fmt.Fprintf. Decide whether to standardize them on slog too, or leave them alone (host already wraps their stdout/stderr).
- Configurable handler: --log-format=text|json on 'gateway run' and 'plugin run' (the latter ties to talon-???, the self-dispatching binary work).
- A shared internal/log package can centralize the handler init + level config + the standard fields ('component', 'plugin', 'agent', 'session_id') that recur across packages.

Out of scope: log levels exposed via config (separate issue if needed), log shipping/aggregation, OpenTelemetry traces.
close_reason: Closed

title: Native chat.history (in-memory)
description: Implement chat.history on talon-gateway. Records each {sessionKey -> []Message} in an in-memory map (sync.Mutex-guarded). chat.send appends both the user message (when received) and the assistant message (when state=final) to the store. chat.history returns the last N messages for the requested sessionKey (param 'limit', default 50). No persistence yet — server restart loses history. Depends on talon-aws-5 (chat.send) since the store is shared.

title: Config-change policy: never auto-restart, never auto-load; HUP-reload where possible
description:
Policy decision (2026-04-27): config writes by talon must never trigger a gateway restart or auto-reload. The user explicitly opted out of file-watcher-based reloads. Where supported, a config field should be hot-reloadable via SIGHUP to the running gateway. Where not, talon's 'config set' output should tell the user a restart is needed.

Scope:
1. Path-class registry — for each known config dot-path, classify as (a) hot-reloadable on SIGHUP, (b) effective-on-next-RPC (no signal needed), (c) requires restart. Initial pass: gateway.* probably (c); channels.* probably (a); models.* probably (b); auth.profiles probably (b); plugins.entries.<x>.enabled requires restart; agents.list probably (a) for non-workspace fields.
2. cmd/talon/config set output — replace the bare 'set <path>' message with a class-aware hint:
   - (a): 'set <path>. Send SIGHUP to the running gateway to apply (or restart).'
   - (b): 'set <path>. Will be picked up on the next RPC.'
   - (c): 'set <path>. Restart the gateway to apply.'
3. Confirm openclaw's gateway actually handles SIGHUP. Today openclaw probably just re-reads on next request; SIGHUP plumbing may not exist. If so, this issue depends on adding SIGHUP support to talon's embedded gateway and/or filing an openclaw upstream issue for the same.
4. The opposite policy — talon must NEVER spawn a file watcher on ~/.openclaw or ~/.talon to auto-detect config changes. Reload is always explicit (signal or restart).
5. Document in CLAUDE.md / docs/architecture.md.

Note: openclaw's existing 'config set' output ends with 'Restart the gateway to apply' regardless of path. We are intentionally diverging from that — talon classifies per-path. PARITY.md should call this out as an intentional difference, not a parity gap.
close_reason: Phase 1 landed: internal/config/reload.go with ReloadClass enum (next-rpc/hup/restart), ClassifyReload registry, ParseReloadClass and Hint. cmd/talon config set emits class-aware hints after writes; --reload override accepts next-rpc|hup|restart for unknown paths. Restart-class entries: gateway.port/bind/auth.*, gateway.tailscale.*, gateway.controlUi.*, plugins.entries.*.enabled, plugins.deny, plugins.load.paths, skills.*. HUP class empty pending talon-gateway SIGHUP handler (Phase 2: talon-f06). Tests cover all listed paths + override parsing + Hint shapes. PARITY.md documents the intentional divergence from openclaw's 'restart to apply' universal message. CLAUDE.md updated with explicit-reload policy + registry pointers.

title: Upstream: openclaw config.schema RPC emits dangling $defs refs
description:
The schema returned by the openclaw config.schema RPC contains $ref pointers to #/$defs/<name> (secretInput, secretRef, account, audioFormatPolicy, route, stt, ...) but does not include a top-level $defs block. Instead, those definitions appear inline inside specific properties (e.g. plugins.entries.feishu.config.secretInput).

Effect on talon: schema compilation via santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 fails with 'json-pointer in ... #/$defs/X not found'. talon's 'config validate' falls back to syntax-only and warns; 'config validate --strict' surfaces the compile error. See ErrSchemaCompileFailed in internal/config/schema.go.

Fix should land upstream in openclaw (the schema generator should either emit a top-level $defs block or rewrite the refs to point at the inline locations). Once fixed, talon will get full schema-aware validation automatically — no talon code change needed.

Reproduce: talon gateway call config.schema | grep -E '"$ref":' | head; jq 'keys[] | select(. == "$defs")' returns nothing.

title: Secrets: macOS Keychain backend, no plaintext in files/env by default
description:
Policy: talon must not store secret values in ~/.talon/openclaw.json or environment variables by default. Replacements should reference a keychain-backed provider.

Current state:
- ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json holds plaintext secrets (gateway.auth.token, channels.telegram.botToken, plugins.entries.brave.config.webSearch.apiKey, skills.entries.openai-whisper-api.apiKey).
- The existing ~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw-gateway-with-1password shim already uses 'security find-generic-password' to fetch a 1Password service-account token from the macOS Keychain, then exports it as OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN. So Keychain is already on the bootstrap path for 1P users.

Scope:
1. Define a talon-side SecretStore interface (Get/Set/Delete by service+account+key).
2. Implement a macOS Keychain backend (Go: prefer github.com/zalando/go-keyring for cross-platform abstraction, fall back to /usr/bin/security CLI shell-out if cgo is undesirable). Linux (libsecret) and Windows (Credential Manager) are bonus targets.
3. Decide the on-disk shape: when 'talon config set' targets a known-secret path, write a SecretRef pointer into ~/.talon/openclaw.json instead of the literal value. Shape options:
   (a) Reuse openclaw's SecretRef ({source, provider, id}) and add a 'keychain' source — requires openclaw runtime support to resolve.
   (b) Introduce a 'talon-secret://service/account' URI form — talon-only, openclaw won't resolve it.
   (c) Bridge: talon writes an 'exec'-source SecretRef pointing at a 'talon secret-resolve' subcommand that reads from Keychain. Works with openclaw today via the existing exec provider.
4. Detect known-secret paths (registry of paths considered sensitive: gateway.auth.token, gateway.auth.password, channels.*.{botToken,token}, plugins.entries.*.config.*.apiKey, skills.entries.*.apiKey, etc.).
5. CLI surface: 'talon config set --keychain' (force keychain backend), 'talon config set' on a known-secret path (default keychain), 'talon secrets list/get/set/delete' for direct management.
6. Migration helper: 'talon secrets migrate' scans ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json for plaintext secrets and offers to move them into Keychain + write talon-overlay refs.

Open questions:
- Native 1Password (op CLI shell-out, or 1P Connect HTTP API, or 1P SDK) vs extending the existing shim. Native gives non-Mac portability and avoids the bootstrap-token-in-Keychain step, but pulls in a heavier dep. Decide before implementation; may end up shipping both modes.
- Coordination with openclaw: option (a) above needs upstream changes; option (c) works today but adds an exec hop.
- Test strategy: keychain access prompts the user. Need a fake-store backend for unit tests, plus an integration-test harness that uses a sandbox keychain (security create-keychain).

Depends on talon-ekv landing first (SecretRef shape parity) so we have the data types to point at.
close_reason: Completed or superseded by current native Talon implementation: first-party Go plugins, TOML/keychain secret flow, and cron CLI/server surfaces have shipped enough that this old bead no longer tracks active work.

title: Transport: replace WebSocket with Connect (Buf)
description:
WebSocket is overkill for talon's actual traffic shape: 95% server-push (chat.delta, agent.tool.start/result, chat.final, channel events) + 5% one-shot RPCs (config.get, agents.list, etc.). Zero true bidi streams (no voice, no client-stream audio). The bidirectional protocol is paying complexity costs we don't use.

Replace with Connect (connectrpc.com/connect) which gives: typed contract via .proto (matches the existing plugin layer), plain HTTP/JSON over POST for browser clients (no grpc-web proxy / Envoy needed), server streaming via HTTP chunked transfer, gRPC wire protocol for non-browser clients, single Go server handles all three.

Why Connect over raw gRPC: the new SvelteKit frontend in web/ would otherwise need a grpc-web proxy. Connect speaks plain HTTP/JSON to browsers directly.

Why Connect over SSE+HTTP: typed contract, codegen for both server and client, matches the proto-first style of the plugin layer.

Migration shape (when ready): define new RPC + stream methods in a .proto; implement Connect handlers alongside the WS handlers (parallel for one release); flip the frontend to Connect; drop WS. Coordinate timing with the frontend rebuild (talon-2dn-and-related).

Must ship before: any further transport investment in WS (e.g. token auth refinements, reconnect logic). Do NOT block: the memory sidecar port (talon-2dn) which is transport-agnostic.

title: talon-gateway: SIGHUP handler that re-reads merged config (Phase 2 of talon-5zx)
description:

Scope:

value: Plugin permissions design (2026-04-27): capability-gated gRPC is the primary isolation layer. Manifest declares what a plugin requests; host enforces. CRITICAL: allow user-grantable escalation — a user can opt to grant specific plugins/agents broader capabilities than the manifest's default ask (e.g. full filesystem access for an admin/deepwork agent). Effective capability set = manifest needs ∪ user grants − user denies. Don't bake workspace-confinement as an invariant; make it the default-on policy that's configurably overridable.

Architecture correction (2026-04-27): talon's PRIMARY goal is being a drop-in replacement for openclaw — that's why we mirror openclaw protocols/methods. Plugin support is REQUIRED, not optional. Two plugin paths must work: (1) existing openclaw Node.js plugins in dist/extensions/ — users shouldn't have to rewrite to migrate; (2) new native-language plugins (Go, Rust, Python, etc.) — preferred mechanism is gRPC subprocess. Native-Go-only providers (current openai/deepseek packages) are an acceptable fast path but NOT the long-term architecture. Channels, tools, providers all eventually need to flow through the plugin layer.

Per-agent tool scope (2026-04-27): tool confinement (currently workspace-only for read/write/bash) is the SAFE default but must be per-agent overridable. A user may legitimately want one agent (e.g. deepwork) to have full filesystem access while keeping another (e.g. research) workspace-confined. When implementing the plugin/tool capability system, design for the per-agent override case from day one — retrofit is expensive.

Project priority (2026-04-27): the user explicitly values that talon is 'so much faster than openclaw'. Speed/latency is a load-bearing differentiator — preserve it when making architectural decisions (favor persistent connections, in-process state, avoiding extra hops; be skeptical of features that add latency even when they look 'cleaner').

Provider integration (2026-04-27): Anthropic in this project goes through Claude Code's OAuth (claude-cli profile), NOT the raw Anthropic API — that makes it the harder provider, not the easier one. First concrete provider should be OpenAI (api_key in ~/.openclaw/agents/<agent>/agent/auth-profiles.json under 'openai:default'). The provider interface is load-bearing and must be designed up-front, not bolted onto a hardcoded first-cut. Order: provider abstraction → OpenAI implementation → chat.send wired through the interface.

UI relocation plan (2026-04-29): the openclaw web UI will move into the talon repo. Until then, edit ../openclaw/ui/ in place for UI work but don't commit to openclaw — leave changes uncommitted, the move will sweep them up. Don't invest in openclaw-side polish (manifest, locales beyond en, etc.) since it's transient.

openclaw plugin trust model (2026-04-27): existing openclaw plugins (Node JS in dist/extensions/) load via require() and have ambient OS authority — fs/net/exec — by design. No way to bolt gRPC capability gates onto them without rewriting. The compat shim subprocess hosts them; they run as the shim does, with full user permissions to OS resources. This isn't a regression vs openclaw (same ambient authority they always had). Native gRPC plugins get the tight capability-gated model; shim-hosted openclaw plugins get crash isolation + in-process state isolation but NOT OS-level isolation. Document this clearly: the trust line for openclaw plugins is 'you already trusted them when you enabled the plugin'. Tighter later via OS sandboxing of the shim subprocess (seccomp/landlock on Linux, sandbox-exec on darwin).
